problem: Current backup create opens an auto-migrating store before taking the copy; normal startup lacks future-schema rejection. Attachment publication and multi-file restore do not yet provide a durable crash-recovery protocol.
Knowledge cutover needs verified backup operations, private file handling, exclusive database ownership and recorded failure/restore evidence. The existing K7a pilot does not prove these guarantees.

risk.rollback: Keep the Git-backed source authoritative until the parent cutover gate passes. Preserve verified pre-migration and current-state copies. After new writes, reconcile those changes or repair forward instead of silently restoring an older snapshot.

scope: Follow S0–S5 in storage-safety-implementation-plan.md: enforce ownership and durable private writes, separate inspection/backup/migration, harden restore, and deliver optional configurable backups with recovery evidence. Automatic backups default off; service policy is configured only through operator CLI startup/service parameters; optional additional user schedules are configured separately within that policy.
Preserve the single local SQLite controller and existing application interfaces; no PostgreSQL or ORM migration is required.

Provide the S6 project-cutover procedure to the shared-project-memory parent. Real-project cutover, host account changes and operational backup destinations require their own concrete rollout scope; saving this plan does not execute them.
Keep code and repository-owned instructions in Git. Avoid two writable sources for migrated knowledge and retain a readable archival/export path.

GUI may list authorized backups and offer on-demand creation and confirmed restore within operator CLI policy. Full-installation operations remain operator-only. GUI/API cannot change service settings, but may manage independent user schedules for permitted scopes, with separate retention and shared bounded execution.
source: Owner storage-safety discussion and request to save an implementation plan on 2026-09-28
title: Secure SQLite migrations, durable storage and recovery before knowledge cutover
validation: Requested backups preserve the supported old schema before migration. A backup failure blocks migration only when pre-migration backup protection is enabled; with backups off, supported migration succeeds without creating backup jobs or requiring a destination.

Supported historical fixtures migrate without data loss; future schemas are rejected before mutation; interrupted initialization and migration recover without silent reset or authentication downgrade.
Crash-point tests cover attachment publication and every restore stage, including disk-full and permission failures, corrupted or incomplete backups, unsafe paths, and foreign-key violations.
Different state directories cannot obtain independent application ownership of the same database; direct CLI creation produces private data files.
An independent restore preserves records, attachment bytes, identities, grants and history; scheduled backup failures and retention are verified against agreed recovery objectives.
Record exact-revision check/build and installed-artifact upgrade/recovery results; distinguish process interruption from unverified power-loss behavior.

Fresh installs and absent configuration keep automatic backups off. Manual creation does not enable scheduling; local-only mode needs no external destination. CLI/service settings survive restart, while disabled scheduling creates no stale-backup alerts or retention deletions.

GUI/API/MCP cannot mutate deployment backup policy. Tenant and organization administrators cannot access global backup operations; operator actions require server-side CLI policy and authentication. GUI on-demand/restore use IDs, idempotency, bounded status and auditable outcomes.

GUI restore validates and confirms whole-installation impact, coordinates maintenance and exclusive database ownership, survives disconnect/restart and never replaces an open database. Restoring a DB cannot change CLI policy.

Changing or disabling a user schedule cannot alter service timing, retention or protected backups. Disabling the service schedule does not disable permitted user schedules. All schedules share one bounded executor with operator-defined per-user limits.

User schedules reauthorize owner, project/data scope and destination at mutation and execution, including after restoring old records. Reject foreign resources and revoked grants; SaaS user exports never include the whole SQLite database or installation credentials.
Concurrent due times, duplicate delivery, restarts, time zones and queue limits preserve attribution and idempotency without backlog bursts or starvation of service backups.
value: Protect authoritative project knowledge during updates and failures, with an exercised recovery procedure and explicit limits on local-agent access.
